description:
FILED s501t (Opus, 2026-10-01) -- split out of #155 when the ARRAY / HASH half shipped.

`tie *FH, 'Class'`, `tie *STDOUT, 'Class'`, `tie *$fh, 'Class'` call TIEHANDLE in perl; PCL announces
  PCL: tie: a filehandle (class Class) is not implemented — it is left untied (see docs/not-supported.md "tie on a filehandle")
and the handle stays untied (docs/not-supported.md "tie on a filehandle").

MEASURED (s473t6a, 2ac855aa): t/op/tiehandle.t perl 67/0, PCL 12/32 with 23 rows NEVER produced -- the file's assertions live INSIDE the tie methods (PRINT, WRITE, READLINE), which never fire.  Everyday: modules/Archive-Tar-Compress (IO::Zlib->new ties *$fh).

METHOD INVENTORY: TIEHANDLE PRINT PRINTF WRITE READLINE GETC READ EOF CLOSE BINMODE FILENO SEEK TELL OPEN UNTIE (DESTROY: never called, USER ruling).

WHAT s501t LEARNED THAT CARRIES OVER:
* The aggregate design ("empty shell + side table", docs/tie-aggregates.md) works because a container's element fast paths have a MISS branch that is free on an empty shell.  A handle has no such branch: every I/O builtin (print, say, printf, readline/<>, getc, read/sysread, eof, close, binmode, fileno, seek, tell, open, write) would need an ENTRY test, and print / readline are the hottest paths.  So measure first: a replica with ONLY a count test at the entry of %p-out-target / the readline entry, benched interleaved with a byte-identical control core (s501t's Step 0 recipe: base extraction's tools/bench-exec.pl + BENCH_RT_B; rows fhread textproc strcat + a new tied-handle row).
* The side table itself (**p-tie-table**, weak EQ, **p-tie-count** defglobal) can hold a handle's record too -- key it by the GLOB (or the stream p-dynamic-typeglob hands over for `tie *$fh`); `%p-tied` is kind-agnostic.
* The tie METHODS go through %p-tie-call (scalar context) / %p-tie-call-list; a missing method dies perl's way through p-method-call ("Can't locate object method ...").
* A glob VALUE and a glob REF are one thing in the box model (#423), so `tie *FH` and `tie *{$fh}` must resolve to the same key -- probe both before keying.
* The announcement (`%p-warn-aggregate-tie`) is the rule-12 fallback until then; its Pl/t guards are Pl/t/tie-01.t row 25 and the section name.
subject: tie on a FILEHANDLE (TIEHANDLE): announced, not implemented -- split from #155 at s501t; t/op/tiehandle.t 12/32 + 23 rows never produced
